fresh_validated_observations.topic: BTC is absorbing additional derivatives deleveraging without retracing the Sep.18 breakout, but institutional-flow confirmation cannot advance over the weekend
fresh_validated_observations.label: LIVE CAUSAL CONTROL / CONSTRUCTIVE BUT WAIT
observed_facts: CoinMarketCap at 01:44 UTC showed BTC near $81,079, approximately flat over 24h and +4.9% over 7d.

CoinMarketCap global derivatives data showed aggregate crypto open interest roughly $421.6B-$428.1B depending endpoint/timestamp, down about 5%-8% over 24h, while BTC 24h liquidations were about $27.1M and down about 90% versus the preceding 24h window.
The large Sep.18 forced-short liquidation impulse has therefore faded while BTC continues to hold near $81K.

Funding remains positive and elevated versus the prior week; CoinMarketCap endpoints disagree on the exact day-over-day funding-rate change because of aggregation/timestamp differences, so no claim of clean funding normalization is made.
U.S. spot ETF markets are closed for the weekend, so there is no new regulated-flow session with which to validate the marginal buyer.
fresh_validated_observations.inference: Price stability while aggregate leverage falls is healthier than a squeeze-only continuation and is consistent with voluntary absorption replacing some forced buying. However the source of that absorption is not identified, and weekend liquidity plus the closed ETF channel make a BUY upgrade premature.
negative_findings: Do not interpret falling aggregate OI alone as spot accumulation; position closures can occur on both sides and endpoint units remain heterogeneous.
Do not treat weekend price resilience as institutional ETF confirmation when the ETF creation/redemption channel is closed.
fresh_validated_observations.decision_support: BTC remains WAIT / tactical confirmation candidate. Upgrade requires completed broad ETF inflows after U.S. markets reopen plus continued price strength without renewed leverage expansion.

fresh_validated_observations.topic: ENA's +22% daily move is not being funded by an active fee-switch buyback; the strongest fundamental catalysts are expectation/supply-structure changes rather than realized token purchases
fresh_validated_observations.label: DAILY BIG-MOVE CAUSAL LAB / NEGATIVE CAUSAL FINDING
observed_facts: CoinMarketCap at 01:44 UTC showed ENA near $0.2081, +21.99%/24h, +47.41%/7d and +73.05%/30d, with roughly $947.6M of 24h volume against about $2.10B market capitalization (turnover about 45%). BTC was approximately flat and SOL down about 2.7% over the same 24h snapshot, confirming a strongly idiosyncratic move.
Ethena governance's Aug.27 fee-switch proposal, confirmed passed on Sep.8, specifies that buybacks begin only when the first USDe circulating-supply milestone is reached; the first rung is $7.5B.
Current public USDe supply snapshots are about $4.8B, materially below the $7.5B activation threshold. The fee-switch framework is therefore not presently generating programmatic ENA buy demand.

The Sep.14 StablecoinX waiver, filed with the SEC and effective Oct.5, releases contractual lock-up/vesting restrictions on its ENA, but dispositions remain subject to Ethena Foundation consent and funding sales require at least five business days' prior notice plus a Foundation purchase option. The legal unlock is therefore not identical to immediate freely marketable supply.

Ethena Foundation previously bought out locked allocations from early investors that had been selling and moved remaining original-investor vesting toward an early conclusion, reducing the recurring monthly-overhang narrative but not burning the tokens.
fresh_validated_observations.inference: The current ENA rally cannot truthfully be attributed to realized fee-switch buybacks. The more defensible causal set is repricing of future value-capture optionality, reduced recurring seed-investor selling expectations, ecosystem/USDe growth and high-beta speculative rotation, with momentum/reflexivity amplifying the move. Because the key governance changes were known before the latest 24h spike, a fresh timestamp-defensible catalyst for the final acceleration remains UNKNOWN.
matched_controls: BTC was roughly flat and SOL negative in the same 24h snapshot while ENA gained about 22%, ruling out broad crypto beta as a sufficient explanation.
USDe supply is growing but remains far below the fee-switch activation rung, separating protocol-growth expectations from actual token buyback flow.
StablecoinX's Oct.5 legal unlock retains sale constraints, so headline unlocked-token quantity is not equivalent to executable sell supply.
negative_findings: Do not label the move 'buyback driven' while the on-chain/economic activation condition is unmet.
Do not label the full StablecoinX holding as an Oct.5 market sell wall; consent, notice, Foundation purchase rights and other legal restrictions constrain realizable supply.
No timestamp-safe fresh catalyst discovered in this cycle explains the final +22% daily acceleration by itself.
fresh_validated_observations.decision_support: ENA remains WAIT / AVOID CHASING. A future BUY case would require actual fee-switch activation/value capture, durable USDe economics, clearer supply realization and a less reflexive entry after extreme turnover.

fresh_validated_observations.topic: The Sep.19 Saudi/Yanbu episode is a useful failed-transmission control: attack attempt does not equal lost deliverable barrels
fresh_validated_observations.label: ENERGY MATCHED CONTROL / CONFIRMS EXISTING RULE
observed_facts: Reuters and Saudi-coalition reporting say a ballistic missile toward Riyadh was intercepted and attempted attacks including Yanbu were thwarted; Reuters separately observed smoke/flames near Riyadh airport but did not establish their cause.
No incremental Sep.19 Yanbu/Aramco throughput or export-capacity loss has been verified at this cutoff.

By contrast, the Sep.8 Saudi energy attacks produced documented fires/operational halts and Brent settled about 0.9% higher at $97.92; the later East-West pipeline outage damaged multiple pumping stations and threatened 4%-5% of global supply-routing capacity, producing much larger crude repricing.
Benchmark crude markets are closed during the current weekend, so no conventional open-market reaction to the Sep.19 claims exists yet.
fresh_validated_observations.inference: The pre-price causal variable is not attack headline count but verified change in effective deliverable supply after interception, redundancy, inventories, rerouting and repair capacity. Sep.19 currently belongs in the no-confirmed-new-barrels-lost control set.
fresh_validated_observations.decision_support: Crude remains WAIT / high event risk; require verified physical impairment plus post-reopen physical/price confirmation before changing direction.
